entries.title: The periodic box and one shell
entries.dek: Fourier space bookkeeping, not cosmology. Pictures that already teach: the periodic box T³ and exact-shell interaction.

images.alt: Teaching diagram: a transparent cube labeled Periodic box T³ filled with a lattice of cyan dots. A circled shell inside. Captions: opposite faces identified; fluid fills the cube — no hole in the center; wavevector space k in Z³; exact shell |k|² = α (one sphere). Footer: this is Fourier space bookkeeping, not cosmology.
images.caption: Periodic box T³ — Fourier space bookkeeping, not cosmology

images.alt: Teaching diagram: Exact-shell interaction. Points p and q on a large sphere (input shell |·|² = α) connect to an output wavevector k = p + q on a smaller shell |k|² = β. A vertical leftover length is labeled |k⊥|² = β(1 − β/4α). Note: when β → 4α the leftover vanishes. Caption on the leftover: this length is the shape of the claimed 4/3 bound.
images.caption: Exact-shell interaction — leftover length is the shape of a claimed bound, not a close
